The proof of the theorem relies on the fact that the moment generating function (MGF) of a random variable is infinitely differentiable at 0 under the given condition that $ 0 \in \text{interior}(\text{integrableExpSet } X \mu) $. This ensures that the exponential of $ X $ is integrable in a neighborhood around 0, allowing for the differentiation under the integral sign.

The key idea is to recognize that the $ n $-th derivative of the MGF at 0 corresponds to the expectation of $ X^n $. By applying the fundamental theorem of calculus for Lebesgue integrals and leveraging the properties of measurable functions and integration, we can interchange differentiation and integration. This leads to the conclusion that the $ n $-th derivative of the MGF at 0 is equal to the integral of $ X^n $ with respect to $ \mu $, as stated in the theorem.
